name: Misere
concept: High risk Gambler with a shady background

backstory.title: Summary
paragraphs:
Michelangelo Fiorichi, born the only son of Aurelio Fiorichi, himself eldest brother of the Fiorichi children and thus official head of the Family, is expected to one day hold a position of power within the Family. Not an offer, not a choice, but a birthright. One he would never be allowed to refuse.
Naturally, a lot of pressure was put upon him, for as long as he can remember. To his father, Michelangelo was never good enough. Not the quickest learner, nor the strongest fighter, not even a natural manipulator, much to his father's despair.

When it became abundantly clear he could not properly control, or even reliably call upon the magic inherent to his bloodline, Aurelio all but expected never to ably raise a worthy heir. Yet, he did everything in his power to shape the soft, naive boy into a prosperous asset for the Family and one day, into an actual leader.

Michelangelo had been taught to 'convince' enemies of the Family, to pry information from their seemingly sealed lips, to make a man disappear without trace, never to be found again, by the time he was twelve. If he dared disobey his father’s lessons, magic served as the easiest and quickest solution – Command, Modify Memory, Geas – Michelangelo grew intimately familiar with every one of those spells. To this day, his memory is faulty, missing parts of his life, that he should be able to remember. A result of too many faces forced to forget, too many holes in his reality.

Serena Fiorichi, his mother, tried everything in her power to keep her son safe. Aurelio, although claiming to ‘love her too much, as to hurt her’, saw it fit to ‘correct’ her behavior, whenever she dared speaking up.
When Michelangelo was 13, he began challenging his father on actions and words, often resulting in the two fighting, usually starting out verbally but ending with Aurelio raising hand or magic against his child. Had it not been for the boy’s standing within the family line of succession, as well as Matriarch Sienna’s favor, Michelangelo might possibly have ended up one of the Family’s puppets – trained assassins, stripped of all emotion, memory and personality. His behavior was chalked up to teenage rebellion and the prospect of him falling in line in the future. He learned about the fate of those, who betrayed the Family not long after turning 14, when he witnessed part of the proceedings, being done to a traitor outside their immediate bloodline.

Around this time, first Aurelio and soon many of the Family started referring to Michelangelo as Misère, a play on the word ‘miser’, wretched and the saying ‘miserere mei, deus’, have mercy, o god. Easily considered a black sheep and scapegoat for younger members of the Family and a hopefully brief disgrace to the Family’s good name by elders, Misère went avoided or mocked by the people surrounding him.

Thankfully, he was not all alone. Lazzaro, his younger cousin, born a Tiefling and thus often target of the Family’s cruelty himself, and Misère grew into good friends, the older often taking responsibility for both or even only Lazzaro’s misdemeanors. A chaotic duo, increasingly skilled in affronting the Family in discreet and creative ways, avoiding blame ever more frequently.
When Carmela joined the Family, a good while after her mother’s return, the three soon grew into a close trio, though Carmela rarely took part in her cousins’ escapades.

When Misère was fifteen he first met Julio, an elf, whose family had promised the Firorichi’s loyalty and service in return for protection and land. Julio worked as a stable-hand for the Family and the two slowly fell in love.

Things took a turn for the worse, when Aurelio discovered his son’s secret. He found the two in his son’s room, following a suspicion, proven correct. Although Misère managed to put invisibility upon Julio, the two did not manage to hide from Aurelio, who forced his son to speak the truth through magic.
The punishment was swift and merciless. Aurelio spoke a command, magic lacing his voice, forcing Misère to take the offered dagger and plunge it into Julio’s heart.
Just before the weapon pierced his lover’s heart, Misère was let off, momentarily realizing the situation. But it was too late, Julio bleeding out through the wound inflicted by him, Misère unable to heal him and Aurelio merely watching in disdain.
The dagger vanished, just as Misère raised it against his father. Aurelio simply caught his son’s attack, fingers locked around his jaw, as inflict wounds drew a messy cut over the left side of his face, taking the young elf’s vision in one eye. Uncaring for his son’s despair, crying over his lover’s lifeless body, his father coldly informed him about the next Family meeting, before leaving him to deal with what occurred on his own.

After this, Misère grew quieter, more reserved around the Family, but simultaneously more hateful towards his father. Anger previously directed at the broken mechanisms of the Fiorichi Family now turned more directly against Aurelio.
It was as a consequence of this quest for destruction that resulted in Misère turning to gambling and alcohol. A natural at the table, he was effectively able to twist and turn the events of a game, so that he would be in total control over what exactly he lost. Always costing Aurelio, disguised as an unlucky gamble, Misère weaponized what turned out to be more than mere skill.
At the table one average night, Misère discovered the exact nature of his supposedly chaotic magic. It was not uncontrolled, but rather tied to chance, like the cards one was dealt in a game of poker.

In the end it was his gambling skills, as well as this very magic that allowed him to get away from his father and the Family for a while. Hearing of a job that needed doing in Zarathur, Misère sought to take it. Aurelio, not trusting his son to not twist this against him in some new creative way, denied his request.
But Misère did not give up that easily, challenging his father to a game of poker for the right to leave.
Although he won the game in the end, Aurelio sought to keep his son by force, trying to modify his memory. But, expecting this, Misère kept a card up his sleeve, capturing the spell instead and finally standing up to his father, in effect being able to leave for Zarathur.
